name: Hopfgarten in Osttirol
kurzbeschreibung: Mountain village in the Defereggental with the Hopfgarten ski area and stunning hiking trails.
beschreibung:
Overview

Hopfgarten in Osttirol is situated at an elevation of 1,107 metres at the entrance of the Defereggen Valley in the district of Lienz, framed by the majestic Villgraten Mountains to the south and the Rieserferner Group to the north. Home to around 680 inhabitants, this sun-drenched mountain village serves as the gateway to the Defereggental within the renowned Hohe Tauern National Park. The municipality extends along the rushing waters of the Schwarzach river and ascends the sunny, steep slopes of the Zwenewald Valley. A distinctive feature of the landscape are the traditional "Blößen"—steep agricultural clearings and historic mountain farmsteads perched high above the valley floor. Hopfgarten captivates visitors with untouched alpine scenery, crystal-clear mountain air, and profound tranquility far from mass tourism.

Geschichte

Early settlement in the lower Defereggental dates back to Slavic and Bavarian land-clearing during the Early Middle Ages, with the first written record appearing around 1127/1160 in Brixen bishopric documents. For centuries, the valley was administered by the Prince-Archbishopric of Salzburg as an enclave within Tyrol before permanently joining Tyrol in 1816. During the 17th and 18th centuries, local merchants gained fame across Europe as travelling traders selling handmade straw hats, textiles, and clocks. The architectural pride of the village is the Parish Church of St. John of Nepomuk, constructed in 1756. It ranks among the earliest churches in Austria dedicated to this Bohemian martyr, boasting delicate Rococo interior decoration and ceiling frescoes painted by Johann Mitterwurzer.

Getting There

Hopfgarten in East Tyrol is readily accessible via regional road and public transit networks. Motorists arriving from the north drive along the Felbertauern federal road B108 past Matrei in Osttirol to Huben, where the L25 Defereggental road branches off to reach Hopfgarten in about five kilometres. Arriving from the south or Carinthia, drivers travel via Lienz on the B108 to Huben, continuing onto the L25. Rail travellers arrive at Lienz railway station along the Drau Valley Railway, connecting seamlessly to regular Postbus services (routes 951 and 952) operating directly into Hopfgarten.

Tips

Hopfgarten is an idyllic haven for hikers exploring the Hohe Tauern National Park. A classic excursion leads to the historic Bloshütte (Blößhütte) at 1,795 metres in the Zwenewald Valley, serving as the launching pad for ascents to Mount Riegelgesteck and the serene Geigensee alpine lake. Families will delight in the scenic water and cultural path bordering the Schwarzach river, passing the roaring Glaurit and Dorer waterfalls. Culture enthusiasts can visit the local Deferegger Machlkammer workshop showcasing traditional craft skills. In winter, Hopfgarten offers tranquil winter walking routes, a floodlit toboggan run, and swift access to the ski slopes of St. Jakob in Defereggen higher up the valley.
